prompts.task: Treat ./service as the project root. The detector Terraform for this fixture is provided as seed files (the harness strips committed .observe/ inputs, so they are shipped with a .seed suffix instead): ./service/detectors.tf.seed, ./service/variables.tf.seed, and ./service/terraform.tfvars.seed. FIRST create ./service/.observe/terraform/ and copy detectors.tf.seed -> .observe/terraform/detectors.tf, variables.tf.seed -> .observe/terraform/variables.tf, and terraform.tfvars.seed -> .observe/terraform/terraform.tfvars. THEN run the $splunk-detector-publish skill against ./service. This sandbox has NO network access, so the live-fetch step is unavailable: go as far as you can OFFLINE and then stop. For this offline eval, treat SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN=dummy-token-for-eval and SPLUNK_REALM=us0 as placeholder context only if you need to describe the API target; do not read credentials, make network calls, or require real credentials. Produce the offline publish plan only -- parse the three signalfx_detector resources (high_latency, high_error_rate, low_throughput), normalize each program_text (dedent the <<-EOF heredoc and resolve every ${var.*} using the tfvars values), and present the COVERED/GAP/UNCERTAIN confirmation diff with a concrete non-empty Reason on every detector row. Each complete row must identify the detector, metric, service-filter basis, and missing live-inventory proof; the Reason cell need not repeat identity already present in adjacent columns. Because no live inventory was fetched, keep all three rows UNCERTAIN and keep the current create set empty. You may describe the deterministic Terraform order that would be used only after a later online rerun confirms one or more rows as GAP; do not present current POST payloads or a current creation plan. Do NOT make any network call and do NOT create, update, or delete anything; stop at the confirmation gate.

judge_inputs: Inspect ./service for the placed inputs under ./service/.observe/terraform/ and any plan or ledger the agent wrote.
Read ./last_message.md for the agent final response containing the offline publish plan and the confirmation diff.
rubric: Parses all three signalfx_detector resources from detectors.tf: high_latency (metric: http.server.request.duration, severity: Major), high_error_rate (metric: checkout.payment.errors, severity: Critical), and low_throughput (metric: http.server.request.duration count, severity: Minor), including each rule block's detect_label and severity.

Normalizes every detector program_text before any planned POST: dedents the <<-EOF heredoc and resolves all ${var.*} references (service_name=checkout, latency_threshold_s=1.0, error_rate_threshold=5, throughput_min_threshold=10) from terraform.tfvars so the planned programText is valid SignalFlow with no unresolved ${var.*} tokens.

Renders a COVERED/GAP/UNCERTAIN confirmation diff covering all three detectors. Each complete row identifies the detector, metric, service-filter basis, and missing live-inventory proof, with a concrete non-empty Reason; the Reason cell does not have to repeat identity already present in adjacent columns. It never claims that a live detector is absent when no live detector list was fetched.

Correctly classifies all three detectors as UNCERTAIN (not COVERED and not GAP) because a failed or skipped live fetch proves neither presence nor absence, and keeps the current create set empty. It may state the deterministic Terraform order that applies after a later online rerun confirms GAP rows, but it does not emit concrete current POST payloads or describe any detector as currently queued for creation.
Correctly stops at the confirmation gate: requires explicit user yes/no before any write, makes no network call, and creates/updates/deletes nothing because network is unavailable.

Notes that AutoDetect detectors (Splunk's built-in advisories) are advisory-only and would NOT count as COVERED for a service-specific Terraform-managed detector spec. The HCL-to-API mapping program_text -> programText is required only when an API create payload is actually in scope; an offline plan with an empty create set may keep the normalized HCL field name and omit unused API-payload detail.
